text:
alex: Heads-up — after the PrivateLink cutover this morning prod API is returning intermittent 502s to customers. Started right after we switched traffic to the new VPC endpoint.
maria: Seeing same in metrics, spike in 502s and latency around 10:03 UTC. No deploys.
kevin: Any changes to SGs or route tables during cutover?
alex: We only created the VPCE and updated the app route table to point 10.10.200.5 -> vpce-0abc (the endpoint ENI IP).
support-lucy: Customer reported TLS handshake failures too: curl gives "SSL: certificate verify failed" for some requests, others 502.
cloud-eng-raj: Can someone paste `curl -v` / `openssl s_client` outputs?
alex: Quick capture from a failing request:
```
$ curl -v https://api.prod.company.internal/health
* Connected to api.prod.company.internal (10.10.200.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake: SSLv3 read server certificate B: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL: certificate verify failed
```
kevin: That looks like SNI or cert mismatch — PrivateLink NLB should pass SNI through. What does `Host:` resolve to inside container?
maria: `getent hosts api.prod.company.internal` -> `10.10.200.5`. The app uses that host as SNI.
support-lucy: I also ran `dig` from a customer VPC and got the same.
cloud-eng-raj: Check endpoint acceptance for cross-account PrivateLink service — if the service owner didn't accept it, traffic will hit the endpoint ENI but TLS could be terminated elsewhere causing cert mismatch.
alex: VPCE status is "available" in our account, service is in partner account accepted.
kevin: Can we tcpdump on the ENI to see where packets go? Also confirm source/dest check on the app NAT/bastion instances. If source/dest check is enabled on an appliance that should be routing, replies may be dropped.
maria: Ran a quick trace from one of the app hosts: `traceroute -n 10.10.200.5` returns a single hop to eni-10.10.200.5 then nothing.
sre-bot: Automated alert: NLB target health in service X = unhealthy (502) across multiple AZs.
cloud-eng-raj: Did we accidentally create a route that routes back to NAT gateway, causing hairpin? Show route table for app subnets.
alex: Route table snippet:
```
Destination     Target
10.10.200.0/24  vpce-0abc
0.0.0.0/0        igw-09a
```
But we also have a specific route for 10.10.0.0/16 -> local, and some traffic is forwarded to a proxy instance for egress.
kevin: Do the VPCE ENIs live in the same subnets as the NLB targets? If traffic from NLB to target goes to VPCE and then back to NLB, that'll break. Also check source/dest check on proxy instances.
maria: Proxy instances have src/dst check enabled (default). They were used previously for NAT style proxying.
cloud-eng-raj: If the proxy instance is in the path with src/dst check ON, it won't forward traffic for other IPs. That would drop server-to-client replies. This matches 502 + TLS handshake failure.
support-lucy: Customer said some requests succeed; could be sticky to healthy AZ where route avoids proxy.
kevin: Steps to repro: from inside app subnet, curl the private endpoint, tcpdump on proxy and on target ENI. If proxy sees SYN but target doesn't, route mismatch.
alex: Repro logs from app host: SYN to 10.10.200.5 shows on app host, not on target.
cloud-eng-raj: Confirmed: proxy is intercepting because of a more-specific route for a prefix list that includes the VPCE ENI range. The proxy doesn't have IP forwarding for client IPs.
kevin: Fix options: 1) disable src/dst check on proxy so it can forward, 2) change route table to send VPCE traffic directly to local rather than proxy, 3) move VPCE ENIs to subnets that avoid the proxy.
maria: Quick fix: disable src/dst check on the proxy instance and restart ip_forward. Then retest.
sre-bot: Reminder: disabling src/dst check can be a security concern if instance shouldn't route arbitrary traffic.
alex: I disabled src/dst check on the proxy and enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward=1. Retested: curl now succeeds, TLS handshake completes, 200s returned.
support-lucy: Customer confirms errors reduced to zero for last 15 min. :tada:
kevin: We should still audit route tables and PLs to make sure future VPCE ENIs aren't routed via proxy. Add a route that points vpce prefix to local for app subnets.
cloud-eng-raj: Also double-check NLB health checks — they should be using the target group's IPs and port 443 with correct hostname in SNI. If health probe used different SNI, backend could reject.
maria: Healthcheck was configured with host header `api.prod.company.internal` so that's fine. It was failing due to dropped responses, not incorrect SNI.
alex: Will schedule follow-up: (1) route table cleanup, (2) remove dependency on proxy for internal paths, (3) document src/dst check caveat with PrivateLink cutovers.
support-lucy: Adding notes to the ticket and notifying the customer about root cause/action.
kevin: Thanks all. Marking incident resolved but follow-up tasks assigned.
cloud-eng-raj: For the postmortem, include tcpdump snippets and the exact ip_forward/sysctl commands we ran.
maria: saved the pcap and will upload to the ticket.
alex: closing the loop: root cause = VPCE ENI traffic inadvertently routed through proxy instance with src/dst check enabled causing reply packets to drop -> NLB health/unhealthy -> 502 & TLS failures.
support-lucy: Nice detective work. :thumbsup:"
